claims.text: Cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr exhibits 8–16% room-temperature tensile ductility.
Cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has a yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C.
Untreated cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has inadequate high-temperature oxygen resistance.
A thin, uniform Al2O3 coating can be deposited on cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr by a process such as chemical vapor deposition.
The applied alumina coating will form a continuous and adherent alumina scale.
A continuous alumina scale acts as a barrier to oxygen diffusion.
The alumina coating produces a stable, slow-growing protective Al2O3 layer.
The protective Al2O3 layer prevents rapid oxygen ingress into the underlying refractory alloy.
Preventing rapid oxygen ingress suppresses oxidation-induced loss of structural and mechanical integrity.
After 5 hours in air at 800 °C, coated equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr will have lower oxidation mass gain than untreated material.
After 5 hours in air at 800 °C, coated equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr will exhibit less surface oxide formation than untreated material.
The coating will preserve room-temperature mechanical properties relative to untreated equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr.
The coating will preserve high-temperature mechanical properties relative to untreated equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr.
The proposed protection is applicable for exposures up to 5 hours at 800 °C in air.
The proposed evaluation applies under static or low-strain-rate loading conditions similar to the referenced mechanical tests.
Performance at higher temperatures, for longer exposures, or under thermal cycling has not been established.
Long-term coating adhesion and effectiveness under repeated thermal cycling are uncertain.
